claim: Tamil Murugan tradition repeatedly associates the deity with red symbolism and the epithet Ceyon/Seyon, 'the Red One'; separate Sri Lankan scholarship identifies the Skanda-Murukan/Kataragama complex as a historically layered shared deity tradition.
bounded_by: The sources support the epithet and the Skanda-Murukan/Kataragama identity complex. They do not establish that red colour itself structures Kandy Perahera ritual or Nallur ritual, nor a direct institutional transmission between those sites.
notes: Run34 forced resolution of the narrower red-god hypothesis; usable only as a bounded cultural-historical callback on top of the already sourced Run29 shared-deity bridge.
